events.title: Works in Public Opening: Riverside Park South
events.description: The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation invite you to the opening of Works in Public in Riverside Park South, celebrating sculptures by Alicia Ehni and Robert Franca.About the Artists & ArtAlicia Ehni, Balancing A Peruvian shaman once told Ehni to carry a lemon in her purse, that it brings great harmony in life and in interactions with others. Two fractured pre-Columbian ceramics carry ancient coastal knowledge, opening possibilities to imagine a different future. Balancing reflects on the fragile relationships between people, nature, and the built environment.Robert Franca, The ChairsThe Chairs explores family as the foundation through which we understand ourselves and the world. Seen through a child’s perspective, the chairs embody imagination, openness, and freedom from conventional rules. Their human-like forms suggest movement and the ability to change. Ultimately, the chairs speak to the importance of finding balance — within ourselves, within families, and in navigating the challenges and uncertainties of an ever-changing world.

events.title: Works in Public Opening: 145th Street
events.description: The Art Students League of New York and the New York City Department of Parks & Recreation invite you to the opening of Works in Public in Riverside Park at 145th Street, celebrating sculptures by Lindsey Francis Jones and Clare Burson.Lindsey Francis Jones, City in Shapes, City in FishCity in Shapes, City in Fish invites viewers into the artist’s visual language through a cityscape of abstract shapes and color. Inspired by the craft and community of printmaking, the work incorporates images of six fish etched onto selected plexiglass, contributed by fellow printmakers and artists: Laurissa Widrick, Felix Bladbjerg, Kait Waldman, Stan Overstreet, Barbara Ganmen, and Scarlett Patino.Clare Burson, Unearthed.UNEARTHED is an installation of three steel forms inspired by the ancient Plain of Jars in Laos. It asks us to consider the inevitable and unexpected ways that history imposes itself on the present. When experienced with its accompanying soundscape, UNEARTHED also reminds us that our shared public spaces are nexus points for an infinite number of narratives that connect individuals and communities across time, those who lived here before us and those who will come after us.
events.venue: 145th and the Hudson River (in Riverside Park)

events.title: NYRR Open Run: St. Marys Park
events.description: NYRR Open Run brings free, 5K weekly community-led runs, to neighborhood parks across the greater New York City area. The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.St. Mary's Park offers a wonderful respite from the hustle and bustle of urban life. Located in the Mott Haven neighborhood in the South Bronx, the park features rolling hills, expanses of green grass, and grand old trees. The site was once part of the estate of Jonas Bronck (1600-43), for whom the Bronx is named. It is one of the largest parks in the area with a pool, playground, basketball courts, an indoor recreation center, picnic seating areas, and more. In the winter, the hills are perfect for sledding. St. Mary’s Park received $30 million from NYC’s Anchor Parks initiative, which will renovate the park’s ballfields, pathways, and amphitheater.

The program is free and open to runners and walkers of all ages, abilities, and experience levels.Evidence of Inwood Hill Park’s formation exists as caves, valleys, and ridges left as the result of shifting glaciers. Evidence of its uninhabited state afterward remains as its forest and salt marsh (the last natural one in Manhattan), and evidence of its use by Native Americans continues to be discovered. Most of the park was largely untouched by wars and development. The park features a hiking trail and the Hudson River Bike Trail, and is one of the best places in NYC to spot a bald eagle. It also includes athletic fields, playgrounds, dog runs, and a barbecue area.The course is three loops on hilly trails and walkways through woods and along a salt marsh.

events.title: Molière in the Park presents: DON JUAN
events.description: Molière in the Park, Brooklyn's home for free world-class theater, invites you to experience legendary French playwright Molière’s most subversive play.Don Juan has abandoned Elvira, whom he seduced into breaking her vows and marrying him. Over the course of a single adventure-filled day, he and his loyal sidekick, Sganarelle, encounter many of the people Don Juan has betrayed. As he seduces women, defies social conventions, mocks religion, and revels in provocation, his appetite for transgression seems impossible to satisfy. Yet the signs are unmistakable: the walls are closing in.Will he truly repent? Or will he just pretend to, like so many around him, and continue down the same path to the bitter end?Translated by Stephen Wadsworth and directed by Drama Desk nominee Lucie Tiberghien, DON JUAN is one of Molière’s most thrilling and provocative masterpieces. A feverish descent from seduction to reckoning, the play blends comedy, tragedy, and the supernatural, pushing Molière’s exploration of hypocrisy and morality further than any of his other works.This free production will once again feature live original cello music by Drama Desk nominated composer Johnathan Moore.RSVPs are encouraged. Learn more at moliereinthepark.org/don-juan-2026
events.venue: Lefrak Center at Lakeside (in Prospect Park)

events.title: Gardening with Ground Covers
events.description: Have you ever wanted an alternative to woodchips or landscape fabric? If so, this is a workshop for you. Ground covers are an excellent way to protect exposed soils while also providing habitat and improving soil stability. In this workshop we will explore a variety of garden situations, plants and expand the definition of “ground covers.” Participants will learn how to select, establish and design with ground covers. No matter the size of your garden, ground covers are a great step towards building a sustainable and more resilient community garden.Register HereNYC Parks GreenThumb hosts this event. We are proud to be the nation’s most extensive urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: Extend Your Growing Season with Low Tunnels
events.description: Urban gardening doesn’t have to stop when temperatures drop! This workshop will teach you how to build low tunnels to protect cold-hardy crops and extend your growing season in small spaces like community plots, backyards, and rooftops. Learn which winter crops thrive in NYC’s climate and how to choose and use materials that fit tight urban gardens. events.title: Woodland Community Volunteer Workday
events.description: Join Wave Hill staff in the Herbert and Hyonja Abrons Woodland to celebrate City of Forest Day! Volunteers will learn about the importance of urban forests while lending a hand in managing invasive species. Gain first-hand knowledge of ecological practices and get your hands dirty while applying them alongside our staff experts. Tasks may include pulling invasive plants or clearing pathways. Please dress appropriately: long pants, layered clothing, and sturdy shoes are required. Gloves and tools provided. This program is appropriate for adults and children under 18 accompanied by an adult. For community groups interested in volunteering please contact volunteer@wavehill.org. Registration required; free daily admission to all registered participants. Questions? Please email us at information@wavehill.org or call 718.549.3200 x251. The Community Woodland Workday will occur in a woodland or meadow setting with mixed-material pathways, varying elevations and possible off-pathway trip hazards. Activities require standing, bending down, and carrying items.

events.title: Forest Bathing
events.description: Engage your senses as you move through the garden on a meditative stroll with certified nature therapy guide Cindy Olsen. Benefits of forest bathing may include cardiovascular strength-building, stress reduction, improved cognitive functioning, boosting the immune system, and creating a deeper connection to nature and the self. Enjoy the healing benefits of the garden, then conclude with ceremonial tea. Severe weather cancels. Space is limited; adults only, please. Registration is required online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251. Questions? Contact us at information@wavehill.org or by calling the number and extension provided above.

events.title: Listening back to Parley
events.description: Join us for a discussion with exhibiting artists Angel Nevarez & Valerie Tevere and legendary hip-hop artist La Roka (Rokafella). Presented in conjunction with the exhibition As far as the ear can hear, this program revisits the artists' collaboration on Parley, one of four works in the exhibition that explores sound across the landscapes of the Bronx, New Orleans, and the Sonoran Desert. Originally commissioned for the 2015 exhibition When You Cut Into the Present, the Future Leaks Out at the Old Bronx Borough Courthouse, Parley, performed by pioneering Bronx b-girl Rokafella (Ana Garcia) and MC Lady L (Lynn Saunders) draws on the sampling techniques and lyrical traditions of early hip-hop to reanimate questions of truth, justice, and hope. Using the musical framework of call and response to form a multilingual dialogue between two voices, Parley reflects Nevarez & Tevere's ongoing interest in framing sound and listening as a transformative practice that connects fragmented histories and collective memory to open new forms of relation. Glyndor Gallery is wheelchair-accessible. There is an accessible, ground-level entrance at the front of the building with an elevator that provides access to the gallery level. The Sunroom Project Space can be accessed with an ADA-compliant ramp. The restroom on the gallery level is all-gender and ADA-compliant. The Glyndor Terrace Garden is accessible via a bluestone path that begins south of the Glyndor House entrance and continues along its western perimeter towards an ADA-compliant ramp located at the Glyndor Terrace Garden’s north entrance.

events.title: Meet the Artists: Tarik Jeremiah Brown and Camille Cooper
events.description: Join us for a Meet the Artist program with Van Lier Community Trust Fellows Tarik Jeremiah Brown and Camille Cooper. At 2PM, Brown will discuss his site-responsive installation, Hush Harbor, which transforms the Sunroom into a contemporary, antebellum hush harbor—a secret gathering place of refuge and worship for enslaved people--through sculpture, moving image, and sound. This project draws on themes of Black survival and faith, exploring ideas related to embodied belief and the relationship between spirit and land. At 3PM, Cooper will discuss his Sun Porch exhibition, SHOWPIECE, which takes up entomological study as a metaphor for the ways trans and gender-variant people are scrutinized and classified by society. Cooper transforms the Sun Porch into an insectarium full of sculptural bugs contextual to the grounds of Wave Hill, fabricated from the packaging of hormone replacement therapy and other trans ephemera. This afternoon program includes conversations with the exhibiting artists and the activation of works on display. Meet the Artist is an ongoing series of conversations between exhibiting artists, the curatorial team, and sometimes invited guests at Wave Hill. As part of the Sunroom Project Space, this program is designed collaboratively with the artists and takes various forms. Meet the Artist offers visitors, the artist's community, and others an opportunity to gain insight into the artist's creative process and the themes present in their work. Registration encouraged but not required, online or by calling 718.549.3200 x251.

Through family-friendly programs, learn about the important role of plants and food in Indigenous cultures. We are open for the holiday on Monday, October 12 and admission is free to all visitors. Meet up at Thomas Jefferson Park in Harlem and enjoy a scenic ride along the riverfront and through the park, ending at the Festival! Free Citi Bikes will be provided thanks to our partnership with Citi Bike, and we can offer a limited number of free helmets. In order to reserve a bike and helmet, please email publicprograms@randallsisland.org. There will be a free Bike Valet provided by Transportation Alternatives so you can safely park your bikes and enjoy the festivities with ease of mind. Citi Bikes will not be included in this valet service, so if you take a Citi Bike to the festival, please find the nearest docking station to park, or ask a RIPA staff member where to dock. You can find the four Citi Bike docks on our interactive map! After the festival, enjoy some time exploring the park’s 9+ miles of cyclist and pedestrian pathways! events.description: Join Howard Garden and NYC Parks GreenThumb for a hands-on volunteer day building new garden beds--no power tools needed! This is an exciting project to be a part of. We'll provide all the tools, training, and guidance to ensure a productive and safe volunteer day! Please wear sturdy work shoes and weather-appropriate clothing and bring water and snacks.Join us for the whole project!Day 1 (Wed. Oct. 7) – Garden Site PrepDay 2 (Sat. Oct. 10) – New Bed BuildingDay 3 (Wed. Oct. 21) – Filling Beds & PlantingHoward Garden was founded in the late 1980's by community activists and artists who've made a lasting impact in the Brownsville community. These gardeners are still active to this day, and are excited to pass along the knowledge and skills gained through decades of environmental stewardship. This is a great opportunity for beginner and seasoned volunteers looking to join a growing garden!Register here!In the event of inclement weather, we'll reschedule this event to Sunday, October 11th.For information about group volunteering, please contact the GreenThumb Volunteer Program at gt.volunteer@parks.nyc.gov. This event is co-hosted by NYC Parks GreenThumb. We are proud to be the nation’s largest urban community gardening program, sustaining over 550 gardens throughout New York City. GreenThumb community gardens are organized, led, and cared for by dedicated volunteer gardeners who critically upkeep them as public green spaces. With GreenThumb’s support, community gardens are centers of environmental justice, ensuring that our city is fairer, safer, and greener for all. GreenThumb’s events are free and open to the public.

events.title: 2026 Spooky Snug Harbor Tour
events.description: Snug Harbor is one of Staten Island’s most beautiful historic destinations. And, if the legends are true, one of its most haunted… This fall, join us for “Spooky Snug Harbor,” a series of nighttime walking tours aimed at shedding light on Snug Harbor’s darkest history. Guided by local history enthusiast Michael Pelczar, founder of Spooky Staten Island, your tour group will hear never-before-published information. Visitors will also have the opportunity to use ghost-hunting equipment during each tour session. Can we make contact with the other side? On October 31st 9:00-10:30 Join our Halloween Special Spooky Snug Harbor tour, you'll journey back in time to learn about murder, mayhem, and hauntings at Snug. You will visit the final resting place of Captain Robert Randall, whose wealth willed Snug Harbor into existence. You'll ponder the mystery of Chaplain Quinn's murder, a crime that gripped the nation. You'll learn about the 19th century disaster that rattled the harbor's buildings... and the unlikely reason its sole survivor escaped. You'll discover a disappearance that sent the institution into a frenzy, and so much more... When: The event runs from 7:30 PM to 9:00 PM. events.title: The History of the Ouija Board
events.description: Dive into the history of the enigmatic Ouija board, and learn how spirit communication became a phenomenon that swept the nation. Today a trademarked game owned and manufactured by Hasbro, Ouija has a history that stretches back to the 19th century. At one time, the "talking board" outsold Monopoly—appearing in silent films, Valentine's Day greeting cards, popular sheet music, and even a Norman Rockwell illustration. Get an up-close look at more than a dozen vintage boards—all with their own unique design and aesthetic—that have dazzled the curious and mystified skeptics for more than one hundred years. When:October 11 | 7:00 pm - 9:00 pmWhere: Carpenter’s Shop (View Site Map and Directions)Admission: General Admission: $30.00Student/Senior: $30.00Snug Harbor Member: $25.00 (With Promo Code)

events.title: Woodlawn Wednesdays: Forest Restoration and Invasive Removal
events.description: Hands-on forest restoration in the Northeast Forest at Woodlawn. We remove the invasive plants crowding out the young native trees regenerating here, and protect what is already coming back. Tools, gloves and guidance provided - no experience needed. Meet at Woodlawn Playground; we walk in together.Dates include Wednesdays weekly from September 2nd - September 30th. Dates are 9/2, 9/9, 9/16, 9/23, and 9/30.Space is limited to 30 volunteers each week. Groups of 6 or more should email noel@vancortlandt.org. Ages 15+ welcome; minors need a waiver.Register for a session

events.title: Birding: Hawk Watch
events.description: Join the Rangers as they hike up the hills of the Bronx-Pelham Landfill, a site closed off to the public. Once known as Tallapoosa Point, the decommissioned landfill is now home to an abundance of wildlife and a popular fly over for hawks and other raptors.
events.venue: Pelham Bay Nature Center (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: City of Forest Day: A Great Tree in a Great Forest
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a walk in this “Forever Wild” preserve, framed by two Great Trees–an ancient white oak and a decomposing European beech. We’ll learn about the lively ecosystems trees create, the history of the forest and its great trees, and roll over logs to see who lives underneath.
events.venue: Independence Ave & W 232nd Street (in Raoul Wallenberg Forest)

events.title: Birding: Fall Migration
events.description: Our Urban Park Rangers will guide you to the best viewing spots in New York City to see fall migratory birds. Birding programs are appropriate for all skill levels and beginners are welcome. Join the Urban Park Rangers on a birding adventure around Pelham Bay Park to look for fall migrants that include warblers, raptors and more!
events.venue: Pelham Bay Nature Center (in Pelham Bay Park)

Featured Artist: Mariel Collard, Karin Giusti, Mark Heller, Anya Hoyer, Ekene Ijeoma, Gail Karlsson, sTo Len, Anthoula Lelekidis, Matthew López-Jensen, Amanda Lovelee, and Laura Nova. events.title: Hispanic Heritage Month: Luminous Luminarias
events.description: Celebrate Hispanic Heritage Month with the Urban Park Rangers as we explore the tradition of luminarias—simple yet beautiful paper lanterns used across Latin America to honor community, culture, and light. Participants will create their own luminarias and learn practical urban gardening techniques inspired by plants commonly found in Hispanic and Latinx communities. This hands-on program blends art, heritage, and nature for all ages.
events.venue: Van Cortlandt Nature Center (in Van Cortlandt Park)

events.title: The Myth of Joe Two Trees
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers in a discussion about the Bronx classic The Last Algonquin while hiking through where the book is set, Pelham Bay Park! Participants will explore the facts and fiction surrounding the story of Joe Two Trees, purportedly the last Lenape person who lived in New York City. All participants welcome, even those who haven’t read the book!
events.venue: Section 2 Orchard Beach (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: It's A Horse of Course Hike and Greet
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a meet-up with our Mounted Unit and their horses! Meet a real horse officer at the Horse of Course program and discover the vital role of horses in city parks enforcement. Learn about how the NYC Parks Mounted Unit cares for the horses, where they live, what they eat, and how the Rangers and Mounted Rangers work together to keep the parks safe. The visit will be followed by horse related crafts in the nature center.

events.title: Prehistoric New York
events.description: Take a trip back in time with the Urban Park Rangers as we hike through Pelham Bay Park discussing the lay of the land in prehistoric times. Learn more about fossils and some geological highlights of New York City.
events.venue: Pelham Bay Nature Center (in Pelham Bay Park)

events.title: City of Forest Day: Great Trees of Inwood Hill Park
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers to celebrate City of Forest Day on a walk-through Manhattan’s oldest growth forest! Learn about the benefits trees provide to our urban environment as we enjoy the shade and identify many of our native trees.
events.venue: West 218th Street and Indian Road (in Inwood Hill Park)

events.title: Spotlight tour: Horticulture
events.description: Dig deep into the High Line’s horticulture with a garden-focused tour! Each led by a knowledgeable High Line Docent, these 90-minute specialized tours offer an immersive look into the High Line’s rich and distinctive horticulture. Participants will gain a deep understanding of legendary garden designer Piet Oudolf’s naturalistic approach to plant selection, how the park’s over 500 species of plants contribute to the thriving ecosystems on the High Line and New York City, and much more.Horticulture tours will be led by docent Barbara Rohdie on September 3 and October 1.

events.title: Third United Lenape / Lunáapeew Nations Pow Wow
events.description: Join Prospect Park Alliance, Éenda-Lunaapeewáhkiing Collective and American Indian Community House for the Third United Lenape / Lunaapeew Nations Pow Wow at the LeFrak Center at Lakeside in Prospect Park. This free, two-day public event welcomes the original Indigenous Lenape peoples who were forced to relocate across the continent back to their ancestral homelands to unite together again to share their cultures with Brooklynites today. Pow Wows are gatherings where Lenape/Lunáapeew and neighboring Indigenous nations socialize and celebrate life. Prospect Park hosted formal Pow Wows from 1916 to 1972. Reviving this tradition in Prospect Park provides the Lenape/Lunáapeew an opportunity to celebrate their culture in their homelands and offers Brooklynites of all backgrounds the chance to enjoy the drumming, dancing, singing, art, crafts and foods of the original stewards of this land.

events.title: Summer on the Hudson: THREAD, a Dance Performance by Kinesis Project
events.description: Join Kinesis Project in our sparkling experiment as we bring THREAD to life along the pathways of Riverside Park South. Enjoy this brand new, large scale work as it leads, surprises and meanders up the River’s side. 5:30pm: Audience Gathers at Locomotive Lawn5:45pm: Performance BeginsTHREAD is the company's third dance work based on research by Dr. Missy Eppes and her colleagues, Dr Stephen Laubach and Dr. Jill A. Marshall.

events.title: Spotlight tour: Art
events.description: Take a deep dive into the sculptures, billboards, murals and other art installations on and around the High Line with a 90-minute specialized tour led by a High Line Docent, a knowledgeable volunteer guide. In it, you’ll learn more about the artists and ideas behind the artworks specially commissioned for the High Line Art program.Art tours will be led by docent Tom Morris on September 10 and October 8.

events.title: Fit & Lit with Janeil Mason
events.description: Fit & Lit is your ultimate dance cardio class, where high-energy movement meets heart-pumping music for a workout experience like no other! Groove to the beats of Soca, Hip Hop, and Afrobeats—genres that’ll keep your feet moving and your spirit lifted. We’ll kick things off with an exciting cardio warm-up that’ll have you dancing, sweating, and smiling all at once. Then, get ready for a quick, powerful HIIT section designed to boost your endurance and metabolism. But don’t worry, we finish strong with a calming mindfulness practice to leave you feeling centered and refreshed.No matter your fitness level, Fit and Lit celebrates rhythm, strength, and self-love—empowering you to dance your way to your best self. Join us, feel the music, feel ENERGIZED and get Fit and Lit!Please wear comfortable clothes and shoes to move around in.Free and open to the public. Advance registration is encouraged. Walk-ups are welcome. The event is rain or shine—the event space is fully covered. In the event of extreme weather, this program may be canceled for the health and safety of our visitors and staff. If a cancellation is necessary, Eventbrite registrants will be notified via email and we will post an update on our website.
events.venue: On the High Line at 14th Street (in The High Line)

events.title: "The Light That Shines Through the Universe": Lectures and Meditations - Monuments to War
events.description: As part of the public programming for Tuan Andrew Nguyen’s High Line Plinth commission, The Light That Shines Through the Universe, the High Line presents a monthly lecture and guided meditation series at the Spur. Presented in partnership with the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, the series invites visitors to engage more deeply with themes central to Nguyen’s work. Each session features a lecture by a scholar, artist, or cultural leader, followed by a guided meditation led by an invited practitioner.The series is hosted by Tashi Chödrön, Himalayan Programs and Communities Ambassador at the Rubin Museum of Himalayan Art, who, in her two decades with the Rubin, has led meditation programs for over ten years and is the current host of the Rubin’s Mindfulness Meditation podcast. Through this combination of intellectual and contemplative practice, the series invites audiences to pause, reflect, and consider the artwork’s historical and philosophical themes through both thought and experience.Closing the series, Nico Rodriguez, deputy director of Monuments Lab, considers Nguyen’s work alongside contemporary artistic approaches to memorialization. The discussion explores how artists reimagine monuments to war by transforming sites of violence into spaces for remembrance, reflection, and collective healing.The lecture will be followed by a guided meditation by Steve Clorfeine, a meditation teacher from the Shambhala tradition with over 40 years of experience.Rain date: October 11, 2 – 3pm

events.title: Historic Harlem Parks Super Hike
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on a hike from Morningside Park through St. Nicholas Park and ending at the Northern tip of Jackie Robinson Park. Learn about the history, geology, and ecology of these beautiful parks.
events.venue: Manhattan Avenue and West 110th Street (in Morningside Park)

events.title: Saltwater Fishing
events.description: Want to go fishing but don’t know how or where to start? Join our Urban Park Rangers for free lessons! Learn how to properly use a fishing rod. Our experienced Rangers teach the ethics of fishing and the ecology of our waterways. All equipment will be provided. Recommended for ages 8 and older.
events.venue: 125th Street and Marginal Street (in West Harlem Piers)

events.title: Nature In A Warming World
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a focused walk through Inwood Hill Park to explore how climate change is affecting local plants and wildlife. Learn how shifting temperatures and extreme weather influence the insects, trees, birds, and mammals we see every day, and discover the changes already underway in this unique urban forest.
events.venue: West 218th Street and Indian Road (in Inwood Hill Park)

events.title: City of Forest Day: Woodland Restoration Walk
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers on a hike through Marine Park’s coastal woodland restoration areas. Learn about the amazing plant and animal species that rely on this unique and threatened habitat.
events.venue: Salt Marsh Nature Center (in Marine Park)

events.title: Disc-golfering Your Park
events.description: Let your competitive spirit soar, both athletically and intellectually as you adventure through Highland Park’s Disc Golf Course while answering nature trivia at each stop. I

events.title: Historic New York: From Streets to Skateparks
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a one-mile historic walk through the Lower East Side and Chinatown to explore the evolution of skateboarding in New York City. Visit iconic locations—including the Brooklyn Banks, Foley Square, Columbus Park, Kim-Lau Square, Alfred E. Smith Park, and Coleman Skatepark—and learn how these spaces shaped the city’s skate culture. This walk highlights the people, places, and moments that helped define skateboarding in NYC.

events.title: Historic New York: Vaudeville Stars of the Evergreens Cemetery
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers in exploring one of Brooklyn’s hidden gems, the Evergreens Cemetery. Learn about the many famous performers from the vaudeville era onwards buried here, and the fascinating history of why they came to rest here.

events.title: Historic New York: Downtown Brooklyn History Super Hike
events.description: Join the Urban Park Rangers for a hike from Fort Greene through Brooklyn Heights. Explore historic sites of early indigenous life and the modern industry of the waterfront. Learn about Brooklyn’s role in the Revolutionary War and the aftermath that led to the borough’s first public parks. Please wear comfortable shoes.
events.venue: Fort Greene Park Visitor Center (in Fort Greene Park)

events.title: Docent led tours of the Historic Conference House Museum
events.description: Take a docent led tour of the Conference House Museum also known as the Billiopp House located on Staten Island, New York and overlooking the Raritan Bay. This two-story grand fieldstone house was built by powerful landowner Royal Navy Captain Christopher Billopp About 1680. He wanted a home that would be an expression of his massive wealth, as well as a symbol of the stability of the colonies. Nearly a century later the Billopp House had become a center of colonial hospitality. Billopp’s great-grandson, loyal to the crown, offered his ancestral family home as the site of a meeting of great importance.It is Named The Conference House because it is the site of the only Peace Conference of the American Revolution. Continental Congress representatives Benjamin Franklin, John Adams and Edward Rutledge met here with British Admiral Lord Howe at his request on September 11,1776 in an unsuccessful effort to stop the American Revolution. The Americans had already written and signed the Declaration of Independence on July 4,1776 and their course would not be altered. Though the group discusses options for a peaceful cessation of hostilities, no agreement was reached and the fighting continued for seven years.Today the Conference House Museum presents an interpretation of an 18th century colonial manor to the general public. events.title: iNaturalist Together Week: Inwood Hill Park Evening Plant ID Walk
events.description: Join NYC Parks and Macaulay Honors College to celebrate iNat Together Week, for an evening bioblitz at Inwood Hill Park, which is part of the Old-Growth Forest Network and accessible via subway. Tina Cuevas, natural areas outreach coordinator at NYC Parks, will discuss restoration activities within NYC Parks and how monitoring plays a large part in how Parks works within our city’s natural areas and beyond. Kelly O’Donnell, lead NYC organizer for City Nature Challenge & director of Science Forward at Macaulay Honors College, will contextualize the data that iNaturalist captures and becomes part of a larger global dataset that helps scientists with their research all over the globe. Participants will learn how to use the iNaturalist app to take data observations of local plants and wildlife. They will be able to learn how to lead their own bioblitzes and engage with the iNaturalist community. Come dressed in sturdy boots or shoes, long sleeves, long pants, and clothing that can get dirty (since we might crouch down on the ground to look at plants).

events.title: Old Stone House: Open Hours
events.description: Come visit the Old Stone House during our public Open Hours! Suggested donation for entry is $3, but no one is turned away for lack of funds. No reservation is necessary for entry.Please note that while our typical hours are Friday-Sunday, 12-4 PM, we host private or ticketed events that may limit public access to the exhibitions. The times listed here are the most accurate reflection of when the House is open to the public. Join us in the upstairs Great Room for new Contemporary Art Exhibits every season.Downstairs we host our permanent exhibit: The Old Stone House: Witness to War: An Exhibit Exploring Conflict from Kieft’s War through the Battle of Brooklyn and the Occupation, 1643-1783Old Stone House: Witness to War is a self-directed exhibit that takes visitors on a journey from the Lenape village of Marechkawick through Dutch colonization and the Revolutionary War era in Brooklyn. Ten themed areas allow visitors to explore this history and consider how war and displacement impacted the community, what choices people had to make at the time, battle strategies, and what makes these issues relevant in today’s world. ACCESSIBILITYThe contemporary art gallery is on display in our Great Room which is up 18 steps with a railing on one side.Witness to War is on the ground floor. The doorway has a 1.5 inch threshold.Public park bathrooms are on the South side of the building. They are on the ground floor but are not currently wheelchair accessible.You will find many oppurtunities to sit and rest throughout the House.The history and art on display should be considered "PG" for complex themes.The atmosphere is always family-friendly and visiting us is a great way for children to practice respectful museum behavior.Tours and walk throughs outside our usual open hours are available by appointment, we'd love to accomidate you! Please contact us with any questions.

events.title: Author Talk with David Rocco: Fireboats of the FDNY
events.description: For the last century and a half, FDNY fireboats have played a vital role in protecting New York City’s waterfront. On Thursday, October 8, the Bayside Historical Society welcomes author and photographer David Rocco for an illustrated presentation exploring the history and evolution of these remarkable vessels.With more than 500 miles of shoreline, New York City has long relied on specialized fireboats to respond to fires along the waterfront and aboard ships. Using historic photographs and images, Rocco will trace their development from the early wooden-hull tugboats to the highly specialized vessels that serve the city today.Rocco has been involved in numerous historic preservation and cultural projects throughout the Hudson Valley and New York City. In 2023, he prepared the successful nomination that placed the retired FDNY fireboat John D. McKean on both the State and National Registers of Historic Places. He currently serves as Vice President of the Fireboat McKean Preservation Project.The presentation will be followed by a question-and-answer session and book signing.Admission is $10 for BHS members and $15 for non-members. Purchase tickets on the BHS website: https://www.baysidehistorical.org/events-1/author-talk-with-david-rocco-fireboats-of-the-fdny.This event is part of Bayside Historical Society's Author Talk at the Castle Series.
events.venue: Bayside Historical Society (in Fort Totten Park)

events.title: Opening Reception: Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures by Billy Cleary
events.description: Van Cortlandt Park in PicturesPhotography by Billy Cleary Opening Reception: Saturday, October 3, 2026 | 3:00–5:00 PMVan Cortlandt House Museum presents Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures, a photography exhibition by Riverdale photographer Billy Cleary celebrating the landscapes, wildlife, and changing seasons of Van Cortlandt Park.A Riverdale resident for more than three decades, Cleary has spent years photographing the places and scenes that define his surroundings. His images capture familiar views of Van Cortlandt Park throughout the year, from tree-lined paths and expansive fields to the park’s ponds, wildlife, and historic entrances. Together, the photographs offer a personal portrait of one of the Bronx’s most significant green spaces through the eyes of a longtime neighbor.Cleary’s interest in photography took on new importance during the pandemic, when he began sharing more of his work on social media. Messages from people who were largely confined to their homes and looked forward to seeing his photographs encouraged him to continue documenting and sharing the landscapes around him. His work has since appeared in group exhibitions with the Riverdale Art Association and in solo exhibitions at the Riverdale-Yonkers Society for Ethical Culture and An Beal Bocht Café.The public is invited to meet the photographer and view the exhibition during an opening reception on Saturday, October 3, from 3:00 to 5:00 PM at Van Cortlandt House Museum. Light refreshments will be served.Please note: The opening reception is for guests ages 21 and over. IDs will be checked at the door.Van Cortlandt Park in Pictures will remain on view through November 8, 2026.Accessibility: at this time, the historic house is accessed using one set of stairs. The exhibition opening reception will take place on the first floor.
events.venue: Van Cortlandt House Museum (in Van Cortlandt Park)

Lottery registration opens on Wednesday, September 16 and closes Thursday, September 17 at 11:59 p.m.Please Note:-You must register each member of your party for the lottery under the same account. Selected participants will be provided details regarding program arrival and other specifics.- There are no indoor facilities, restrooms or drinking fountains on Hart Island. There are portable restrooms on the island.- This tour covers historical context of Hart Island and is about two hours of walking, some parts on uneven terrain. Please dress appropriately for the weather and the terrain.- Program may be cancelled due to inclement weather at the discretion of ferry operations.

events.title: Salon: An Art & Fashion Book Club
events.description:
Join us for the inaugural edition of Salon: An Art & Fashion Book Club! 

Our first book will be The Beautiful Fall: Fashion, Genius, and Glorious Excess in 1970s Paris by Alicia Drake. It's a comprehensive biography of the late designer, Karl Lagerfeld, and his infamous rivalry with Yves Saint Laurent.

Every month, we'll gather and discuss some of the best nonfiction books covering art and fashion and discover notable moments throughout the history of fashion. Marmalade in Brooklyn will provide the cozy, salon vibe, and we'll have the types of French wine on hand that we might've found Yves Saint Laurent sipping at Cafe de Fleur in the seventies. 

For our first gathering, books can be ordered through Word Bookstore for a 10% discount.

Here's a synopsis of September's book from the publisher and some reviews.... 

In the 1970s, Paris fashion exploded like a champagne bottle left out in the sun. Amid sequins and longing, celebrities and aspirants flocked to the heart of chic, and Paris became a hothouse of revelry, intrigue, and searing ambition. At the center of it all were fashion's most beloved luminaries - Yves Saint Laurent, the reclusive enfant terrible, and Karl Lagerfeld, the flamboyant freelancer with a talent for reinvention - and they divided Paris into two fabulous halves. Their enduring rivalry is chronicled in this dazzling exposè of an era: of social ambitions, shared obsessions, and the mesmerizing quest for beauty.

"Deliciously dramatic... The Beautiful Fall crackles with excitement."-New York Times Book Review

"Fascinating." -New York Times

"Addictive." -Philadelphia Inquirer

"It's like US Weekly, 1970s style." -Gotham

"A story constructed as exquisitely as a couture dress. . . . It moves stylishly forward, with frequent over-the-shoulder glances at some very dishy background." -Boston Globe

events.title: Learn to Create Over the Top Sundaes
events.description:
Join Joe Calderone, Chef and Creative director of NYC institution, Serendipity3, as you learn to learn to build your very own ice cream sundae, layer by layer!

Known for its outlandish and whimsical creations, Serenditpity 3 has been an enclave for artists like Andy Worhol, celebrities like Marilyn Monroe and of course, dessert-lovers since 1954.

This hands-on class is the perfect opportunity to let your inner child run free as you’re surrounded by eclectic decor like Tiffany lamps and an Andy Warhol puppet hanging from the ceiling - the perfect environment for making an over-the-top sundae!

Before bringing your dream sundae to life, you’ll have the opportunity to brainstorm ideas while talking through your vision with Chef Calderone.

Throughout the process, Chef will be going around to assist not only with building the sundae, but will also offer suggestions on how to garnish, drizzle and layer the sundae it based on what speaks to you.

After building your sundae, you’ll get to present and show off your creation to the rest of the group before mingling and hearing stories on Chef and Serendipity3.

Guests will round out the sweet day by perusing Serendipity3’s wondrous gift store.

What You’ll Learn

Open Studios at the Ke-nee-go-keshek Fine Arts Workshop is a casual and low-stakes creative coworking club, bringing artists and hobbyists together to share in the joy of creation. 

The space is open to all, our one condition is: No Spectators! Please come ready to contribute to the creative energy and life of the space. This doesn’t mean that you have to be talkative or outgoing (though this is welcome) it just means that you have to make art while you’re here.

We’ll all work on our own projects/expressions and enjoying one another’s company in the process. We can chat or share the space wordlessly, listening to music or a podcast.

There are free supplies available for you to paint, write, and sculpt with. You are encouraged to bring your own materials or projects-in-progress, or start something new if you’d like. Writers, I know what you’re wondering- and yes, laptops are welcome! We ask that you try to stay away from admin work and tasks that do not bring you joy or fill your cup during this time.

events.title: 10/4 | First Sunday: Dim Sum, Mahjong
events.description:
Growing up in LA, dim sum followed by mahjong was a weekly ritual. A group of five families would gather for dim sum lunch before caravanning to one of our homes for hours of mahjong that stretched into the wee hours of the morning.

Inspired by this tradition of ritual and gathering, we're continuing the "First Sundays" series at Nin Hao, with an all-you-can-eat dim sum buffet format.

Come join us for an afternoon to learn Hong Kong-style mahjong and connect with friends and neighbors over dim sum and tea.

What to Expect:
1:45PM to 2:15PM: Buffet
2:15PM to 2:45PM: Learning fundamentals and then set up your first game
2:45PM to 4:15PM: Guided open play to apply what you've learned

Just as I learned this game as a way to hold onto community and tradition, this workshop offers more than just rules and strategy. It's an invitation to embrace the ritual of gathering, playing, and being together.

No prior knowledge needed, our workshop is designed for beginners, though experienced players are welcome to join and refresh their skills.

🀄 Guided instruction on Hong Kong style mahjong fundamentals
🀄 Take-home cheat sheet to reference for future games
🀄 Hands-on practice in a supportive environment
🀄 All-you-can-eat dim sum buffet featuring a rotating selection of Nin Hao's classics, including vegetarian-friendly options
🀄 A pot of premium loose leaf Chinese tea to enjoy while you play

About Your Instructor:
Veronica Chan is the founder of Vermilion Mahjong Club, where she hosts intimate workshops and monthly gatherings to foster connection and community around the mahjong table. She brings a warm, accessible approach to teaching this traditional game, making it approachable for newcomers while honoring its rich cultural heritage.

Payment: Your $35 payment today guarantees your spot at the event. Participants will receive a separate restaurant bill of $35 for the dim sum buffet as well as any a la carte drink orders at the end of the afternoon. Tax and gratuity for buffet & drinks is not included.

Cancellation Policy: The $35 teaching fee is non-refundable and non-exchangeable, although if you are not able to make it you will not be charged the $35 buffet fee. Be sure to check your calendar before booking. If you're unable to attend, you may transfer your ticket to a friend.

Seating: Please let me know in advance if you are coming with other friends so I can try my best to seat you together. The buffet is self-service so you can eat at your own pace throughout the session.

Different Mahjong Styles: We will be learning and playing Hong Kong-style (the most popular Chinese mahjong style), not American-style.

3 clues to identify which style is which:

American: Sets include Joker tiles
Chinese (including Hong Kong): Sets do not include Joker tiles

American: Eligible winning hands change annually
Chinese (including Hong Kong): Rules and eligible winning hands do not change annually

American: Sometimes spelled Mahjongg, with two g's
Chinese: Most often spelled Mahjong, with just one g

events.title: Breathwork for somatic & emotional release 10/03
events.description:
Most of us have spent years trying to think our way out of pain and suffering that lives in the body. No matter how self-aware we become through talk therapy and introspection, we can still feel stuck if we neglect our body. 

Instead of starting with the story, Facilitated Breath Repatterning (FBR) addresses the nervous system directly. Connected breathwork shifts your physiology, allowing for subconscious emotional and somatic processing, release, and discovery, much like a therapeutic psychedelic journey. 

FBR is different from other breathwork modalities such as Holotropic or Wim Hof because it incorporates therapeutic attuned touchwork which can create deeper release and nervous system change. The circles tend to be much smaller and more intimate.

Sessions tend to be surprising — big emotions can come up, the body can unwind old trauma, or sometimes it is quiet and restorative. Each journey looks different, but most people report a sense of coming home to themselves through their breath. 

All of it is welcome and no prior experience with breathwork is necessary.

events.title: Feed the Village! Ăn Nhiều
events.description:
We’re creating a space where people can spend a few hours being authentically loved and giving love. Creating a space that is warm and community is brought together. So many different talents and cravings all put into one table, everyone hoping for a chance to spin the turntable.

	Food culture is centered around how people eat. How food is shared. Social eating takes place in so many different BIPOC cultures where community and family are at the forefront. Being able to share food with those that you love is not a luxury, but a standard of practice. This is meant to be a table that is created so that everyone has a seat and a plate. 

Think dinner tables that are too full with dishes meant to be shared, think plates being passed around, think too many chopsticks for the amount of people sitting. Hear the loud chatter of people gathered together, listen to the conversations of the people next to you, feel the warmth of bodies sitting too close together. 

The first dinner is to honor Jonathan. Everything after is to honor the vision he had. 

	The first dinner is meant to showcase the barebones roots. Basic Vietnamese-inspired menu, mainly shareables and eaten family-style.

“Tell me what you eat, and I’ll tell you who you are.” – Jean Anthelme Brillat-Savarin

events.title: Llama & Alpaca-My-Appetite: Trail Side Taste Of Peru
events.description:
Trade city streets for open fields and fresh country air as we head out of town for a one-of-a-kind countryside escape. On this adventure, you won’t just be hiking! You’ll be trekking alongside llamas and alpacas, your new four-legged trail companions.

We’ll arrive at the farm, meet our fluffy hiking partners, and set off on a relaxed, scenic walk through rolling hills and peaceful landscapes. These gentle, curious animals make the experience equal parts calming and unforgettable (and yes: very Instagram-worthy).

After our trek, we’ll shift from trail time to taste time with a trail-side taste of Peru: a delicious nod to the animals’ South American roots. Expect a curated Peruvian-inspired food experience that brings bold flavors and countryside vibes together. Fresh air, good company, and incredible bites… this is the kind of pairing we like.

Whether you’re here for the animal energy, the cultural flavors, or just a wholesome day outside, this one hits on all levels. Fluffy hiking partners. Bold flavors. Countryside energy with a South American twist.

Event Details:
10:00 AM – Meet at The Standard Biergarten
10:30 AM – Depart NYC
12:00 PM – Arrive at Farm + Llama & Alpaca Trek
3:15 PM – Conclude Trek + Trail Side Taste of Peru
5:30 PM – Depart for NYC
7:00 PM – Arrive back in NYC
(All times are approximate and subject to traffic and group pace.)

What’s Included in Your Ticket:
Round-trip transportation
Guided farm hike
Llama & alpaca trekking experience
Beverages for the ride home
OUTSIDERS host on-site

What to Bring:
Proper hiking boots (required)
Plenty of water
Weather-appropriate layers
Big appetite
Card/cash for post-hike meal

Important Notes:
Proper hiking boots are required.
Our adventures are full-day experiences. We do not recommend scheduling other activities that day, as return times can vary.

Proper footwear is mandatory. Unsafe attire may result in denied participation for safety reasons.
If you are not dressed in weather-appropriate gear or your attire is deemed unsuitable for the activity, we have the right to turn you down for the safety of the group and yourself.

If you have any medical conditions or injuries that might prevent you from completing the trip, please consult your physician to confirm your ability to partake in the activities safely.
A signed waiver is required.

events.title: The Annual Atlantic Antic
events.description:
A Brooklyn institution, The Annual Atlantic Antic™, produced by the Atlantic Avenue Local Development Corporation, is the oldest and largest street festival in Brooklyn and a joyful experience, looked forward to by residents of Brooklyn and beyond each year.  

Strolling the avenue from Fourth to the Waterfront on a lovely fall day, is a celebration of ethnic tastings, fine arts and crafts from around the world, non-stop music and entertainment, and just pure fun.  You’re likely to meet up with old friends or perhaps make new ones. You’ll want to spend the day, as there is just so much to see and do!

events.title: Sketching @ the Museum at FIT
events.description:
Welcome to queer museum sketching, hosted by Aubrey (they/them)! We meet once a month to sketch at a free/pay-what-you-can museum in NYC. 

This month we’re meeting at: 

✨MUSEUM AT FIT!✨

I'm so excited about this because I think sketching clothes will be so fun. And it'll be sick to see student work! 

Tickets are FREE! 

BYO supplies
Share the invite + bring friends! 
Please update your RSVP so I can communicate where we are in the museum if you’re running late. 

🦋 Sketching is for everyone ~ whether you’re a pro artist or hobbyist or haven’t drawn before, sketching at museums is a great way to engage more closely with the exhibit and take inspiration from what’s in front of you.
